translationRepairs: Corvée labor was restored for descendants of the Kong clan and for descendants of the main lines of Yan and Meng.
Corvée labor was remitted for descendants of the Kong clan and for descendants of the main lines of Yan and Meng.
復…徭役 here is a privilege of exemption (復除), matching the surrounding honors for the Kong, Yan, and Meng lines; “restored” would reinstate labor duties and reverse the Chinese.
The emperor was pleased and that same day promoted him to Junior Mentor to lecture the heir apparent.
The emperor was pleased and that same day specially promoted both men to Junior Mentor to lecture and read with the heir apparent.
李賢 recommended both 公恂 and 司馬恂; 同日超拜少詹事 and 聖賢子孫為汝子傅 show a same-day leap promotion of both men to lecture and read for the heir, not a singular “him.”
The emperor was pleased and on the same day promoted him to Junior Mentor, to attend the Eastern Palace in lecture and reading.
The emperor was pleased and on the same day specially promoted both men to Junior Mentor, to attend the Eastern Palace in lecture and reading.
The same sentence promotes both men named in the preceding memorial; 超拜 is a special leap appointment omitted by “promoted him.”

In the sixth year bandits broke out in Shandong; Wenshao and Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang proposed fortifying Qufu and moving the county seat to protect the temple, but the plan was never carried out.

In the sixth year bandits broke out in Shandong; Wenshao and Grand Coordinator Zhao Huang proposed fortifying Queli and moving the Qufu county seat to protect the temple, but the plan was never carried out.
城闕里 is a proposal to wall Queli; 遷曲阜縣治 is a separate move of the Qufu county seat. Fortifying “Qufu” collapses the two places.
Kong Yanchang, whose courtesy name was Chaowu, was from Xi'an in Quzhou and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of the Sage.
Kong Yansheng, whose courtesy name was Chaowu, was from Xi'an in Quzhou and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of the Sage.
彥繩 romanizes as Yansheng; 繩 is shéng, not cháng. “Yanchang” is a naming error.
Kong Yanchang, courtesy name Chaowu, was a native of Xi'an in Quzhou and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of the Sage.
Kong Yansheng, courtesy name Chaowu, was a native of Xi'an in Quzhou and a fifty-ninth-generation descendant of the Sage.
The literal field repeats the same 彥繩 romanization error as the idiomatic sentence.
In the ninth year of Wanli his stepmother, the Guo clan, accused Shangxian.
In the ninth year of Wanli his stepmother née Guo accused Shangxian.
庶母郭氏 is Shangxian’s stepmother, a woman née Guo; the appositive “the Guo clan” makes the clan the accuser.
Soon afterward, because Xihui was not born of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was reappointed instead.
Soon afterward, because Xihui was not born of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was appointed instead.
After 希惠 is rejected as 非嫡子, 仍以希仁長子議為之 assigns the doctorate to Yi for the first time; “reappointed” invents a prior tenure.
Before long, because Xihui was not the son of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was again appointed.
Before long, because Xihui was not the son of the principal wife, Xiren's eldest son Yi was then appointed.
仍以 marks filling the post with Xiren’s eldest son after Xihui, not a second appointment of Yi.
Thereupon the Jiangxi grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner reported Zhicui's name; he was ordered to return to Jiaxiang and perform sacrifices in ordinary dress.
Thereupon the Jiangxi grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner reported Zhicui's name; he was ordered to return to Jiaxiang and perform sacrifices in scholar's dress.
衣巾 is the scholar’s robe and kerchief for sacrificial service, not ordinary civilian dress.

Hao's son Jizu, styled Shengzhi, had been partly blind from youth; a Jiangxi kinsman named Gun tried to seize the post but was impeached by supervising secretary Liu Buxi and censor Liu Guangguo; Gun was removed from office and Jizu retained charge of the sacrifices.

Hao's son Jizu, styled Shengzhi, had suffered from eye disease from youth; a Jiangxi kinsman named Gun tried to seize the post but was impeached by supervising secretary Liu Buxi and censor Liu Guangguo; Gun was removed from office and Jizu retained charge of the sacrifices.
少病目 records eye illness from youth; “partly blind” adds a degree of sight loss the Chinese does not state.
呂子銓 is the same father–son formula as 銓子則顯 and 則顯子於陛, not a compound name Lü Ziquan.
The literal English likewise fuses 呂 and his son 銓 into one invented personal name.

In Chongzhen 16, on Duke Yinzhi's recommendation, an edict made Yubi Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, hereditary for his line, and granted more than sixty qing of land in Sishui County and Jining Prefecture plus thirty-one temple households to support his sacrifices.

In Chongzhen 16, on the recommendation of Kong Yinzhi, Duke of Yan Sheng, an edict made Yubi Hanlin Doctor of the Five Classics, hereditary for his line, and granted more than sixty qing of land in Sishui County and Jining Prefecture plus thirty-one temple households to support his sacrifices.
The source names 衍聖公孔蔭植; “Duke Yinzhi” drops both the Kong surname and the Yan Sheng dukedom.
Zhu Ting, styled Mengling, was a ninth-generation descendant of Zhu Xi and his family had long lived at Zixia Isle in Jian'an County, Fujian.
Zhu Ting, styled Mengling, was a ninth-generation descendant of Zhu Xi. His family had long lived at Zixia Isle in Jian'an County, Fujian.
世居 follows 朱梴…九世孫也 and describes Ting’s line at 紫霞洲, not Zhu Xi’s household; the coordinated “and his family” can attach to Zhu Xi.
